contents.Text: [[[underline:Soft Purple]]] ≈ Start/Progress
[[[underline:Soft Yellow]]] ≈ Automatic Duplicate Detector
[[[underline:Dark Blue]]] ≈ Deduplication Threads
[[[underline:Light Green]]] ≈ Data Migration
[[[underline:Pale Orange]]] ≈ Select Similarity Mode
Use this control to start the [[[strong:Duplicate Detector]]] manually.
[[[warning:Note:]]] A progress bar is displayed while the scan is running.
[[[warning:Note:]]] The only way to abort the duplicate detection process is to close the application.
[[[warning:Note:]]] There is no other way to stop the scan.
After the [[[strong:Downloader]]] has finished, this will call the [[[strong:Duplicate Detector]]] automatically.
[[[warning:Note:]]] The automatic scan uses the currently selected [[[strong:Select Similarity Mode]]] setting.
Sets the number of CPU threads used by the [[[strong:Duplicate Detector]]] while scanning for duplicate files.
The slider allows you to select between [[[strong:1]]] thread and the maximum number of available CPU threads.
Using more threads will reduce scan times and increase CPU usage when additional CPU cores are available, but may affect the performance of other applications.
Controls which metadata is preserved when the [[[strong:Duplicate Detector]]] replaces an old song with a new one.
Resets all tickboxes to their default state. This does not remove or change metadata from any songs.
Each tickbox represents a metadata field that can be copied from the old song to the new song.
When a tickbox is selected, the [[[strong:Duplicate Detector]]] checks whether the old song has a value for that field.
If it does, and the corresponding field on the new song is empty or [[[strong:null]]], the value is copied to the new song.
If the new song already has a value for that field, it is left unchanged.
This helps preserve metadata when duplicate songs are replaced.
Selects how the [[[strong:Duplicate Detector]]] compares files and determines whether they may be duplicates.
[[[strong:• Lite]]] Matches only titles that are nearly identical.
[[[strong:• Standard]]] Handles minor differences such as capitalization and punctuation.
[[[strong:• Balanced]]] Handles common variations such as different word order and small typos.
[[[strong:• Deep Scan]]] Handles inconsistent formatting commonly introduced by different sources.
[[[strong:• Advanced]]] Handles significant differences in title structure.
[[[strong:• Aggressive]]] Prioritizes audio content when filenames or titles do not match reliably.
[[[strong:• Maximum Recall]]] Matches files without shared name information by comparing their audio content.
[[[strong:• Exhaustive]]] Forces every potential file pair to be compared. This provides the broadest comparison but may take substantially longer to complete.
[[[warning:Note:]]] The similarity modes use overlapping comparison methods, so their results may overlap. However, no single mode is guaranteed to find every duplicate.
For the best chance of finding all possible duplicates, use [[[strong:Exhaustive]]] or run every mode from [[[strong:Maximum Recall]]] through [[[strong:Lite]]].
The [[[strong:Duplicate Detector]]] uses the [[[strong:cached_fingerprint]]] field from the [[[button:Metadata Editor][../../Metadata Editor]]] cache.
This field stores generated [[[strong:audio fingerprints]]], which help compare the actual audio content when filenames or titles differ.
Fingerprints are [[[strong:cached on-demand]]], so they are generated only when a detection mode requires them.
Once cached, they speed up future scans by avoiding unnecessary recalculation.
Stricter modes, such as [[[strong:Lite]]] and [[[strong:Standard]]], perform [[[strong:fewer comparisons]]] and therefore cache fingerprints for fewer files.
This creates a [[[strong:smaller fingerprint database]]] while limiting comparisons to files that are more likely to be duplicates.
[[[warning:Note:]]] The [[[strong:Duplicate Detector]]] is tied directly to the [[[strong:Search]]] database, not to the path used by the [[[strong:Downloader]]].
It scans the files included in the current [[[strong:Search]]] scope and uses that database to cache their fingerprints.
Wherever the [[[strong:Search]]] is pointed, the duplicate detector scans the files available in that search scope.
Changing the [[[strong:Search]]] scope changes which files the detector scans.
